summary: Delayed initial-token emission observed for chat completions after runtime/model rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Customers reported a significant increase in Time-To-First-Token (TTFB) for chat completion requests immediately after the March 9th runtime+model catalog rollout (runtime v1.4.0 + redwood-v2-7b). The symptom is a 2-4x delay before the first token is emitted, while downstream token streaming and overall token generation remain normal once the first token is produced.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat UX stalls for 1-3 seconds longer than baseline for short prompts.
- Observed for a subset of sessions (~12% of BrightLeaf traffic) using redwood-v2-7b variants.
- Affects enterprise customers with stricter latency SLAs.

Environment:
- Production (us-east) on hosted Redwood API.
- Runtime version: 1.4.0 rolled 2026-03-09 02:10 UTC.
- Model variants: redwood-v2-7b, redwood-v2-7b-quant.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1. Send a chat completion request using default streaming with short prompt (~15 tokens) and max_tokens 150.
2. Observe server accepts connection; initial response (first token) delayed 1.0-3.2s compared to baseline.
3. Subsequent token pacing is normal.

Logs & metrics attached in investigation notes below.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Priya Shah: Customer BrightLeaf opened a ticket reporting slower chat responsiveness after we shipped runtime 1.4.0. They provided example request IDs and session timestamps. Provided initial troubleshooting checklist and requested logs. Marked P1 due to enterprise SLA.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Collected request traces for three example request IDs. Trace shows long gap between TCP handshake/headers and first chunk of streaming payload from runtime host. No 5xx errors. Putting temporary rate-limit bypass for BrightLeaf to rule out quota throttling.

2026-03-10 11:30 - Aria Chen (Serving Eng): Reproduced locally against v1.4.0 with redwood-v2-7b: intermittent 800-1200ms delay before first token for short prompts. Hypothesis: new kernel-selection path or batching threshold introduces scheduling delay for small-seq requests when KV-cache is warm. Opened PR to add timing logs in kernel selection (see PR 478).

2026-03-10 14:02 - Liam O'Connor: Experimented with disabling prefix/KV caching for affected sessions — observed TTFB drop back to baseline in canary tests for short prompts. When caching enabled, delay reappears. This suggests interaction between cache path and runtime scheduling.

2026-03-11 02:20 - Aria Chen: Found that the runtime's new kernel selection defers scheduling when estimated token generation work < batch_threshold and kv_cache_size > 1MB, making small short-prompt chat requests wait for a batching window (up to 1s) to try to coalesce work. This was introduced to improve throughput but regresses TTFB on short interactive requests.

2026-03-11 08:40 - Priya Shah: Shared workaround with BrightLeaf — forced their sessions to use model variant redwood-v2-7b-legacy (pinned to runtime 1.3.x) via per-customer routing policy. BrightLeaf confirmed UX improved. Recording this as mitigation while we prepare a patch.

2026-03-12 13:10 - Aria Chen: Patch prepared to adjust batching heuristics: lower batching coalescing window for interactive tag and add explicit 'min_latency' path for pinned enterprise customers. PR 512 created; running CI and canary against prod-us-east on a 5% traffic slice.

2026-03-12 18:25 - Liam O'Connor: Canary rollouts show TTFB returning to baseline for interactive-tagged requests. No increase in GPU utilization beyond expected. Plan to promote patch to full rollout tonight with monitoring.

2026-03-12 22:05 - Priya Shah: Notified BrightLeaf of planned permanent fix and confirmed they are okay keeping routing to legacy variant until deployment completes. Follow-up items: update runbook and add an automated regression test for TTFB on short prompts.

2026-03-12 23:50 - Aria Chen: Post-deploy observation: full rollout completed. TTFB metrics for redwood-v2-7b in us-east show median drop from 540ms to 180ms for 10-20 token prompts. Closing investigative work; will keep ticket open for postmortem and runbook updates.
investigation_notes: Summary of findings: regression introduced by runtime v1.4.0 kernel selection + batching heuristic which attempts to coalesce small requests when KV cache is present, adding up to 1s delay before scheduling. Disabling KV cache returned baseline. Root cause: aggressive coalescing window combined with improper 'interactive' workload tag handling. Impact limited to short-prompt interactive chats and only when KV cache size exceeded threshold. Resolution: updated batching policy (interactive fast-path) and per-customer routing defaults to avoid automatic batching for pinned enterprise interactive sessions.
resolution:
Mitigated: provided immediate routing to legacy runtime for affected customers; deployed patch to runtime adjusting batching heuristics and prioritizing interactive flows. Post-deploy monitoring shows TTFB restored to baseline.
Permanent fix: PR 512 merged to main and backported to 1.4.x branch.
Follow-ups: add TTFB regression test in CI, update rollout checklist to include interactive latency benchmarks, and add a console alert that triggers when median TTFB for chat endpoints increases >30% over baseline.
